# cycles-vs-eevee-decision

Purpose: Pick Cycles, Eevee, or Workbench for a render based on quality bar, time budget, and feature requirements (caustics, subsurface, etc.). Note: Eevee was named Eevee Next on Blender 4.2-4.x only.

Pick the render engine upfront based on quality + time tradeoff and feature requirements. Avoid the "use Cycles always" / "Eevee is faster" oversimplifications.

Metadata: Contract `v1.0.0` | Category `render-and-output-decisions` | Role `render-engine-tradeoff-selector` | Tier `L0` | Runtime default `Not Run` | Artifact default `Not Produced` | Mutation `downgrade_only`

## When to use & trigger cues
- before render
- when feature support drives engine choice
- when time vs quality tradeoff matters
- when previous render was wrong engine
- Trigger phrases: "Cycles or Eevee", "what render engine", "is Eevee enough", "render is too slow"

## When not to use (delegation boundaries)
- for a known repeat render (engine already chosen) → use `blender-lighting-material-planner` (`references/skill-blender-lighting-material-planner.md`; engine already chosen)
- for non-render work (modeling / animation prep) → use `output-format-decision` (`references/skill-output-format-decision.md`; modeling / animation prep)

## Input & output contract
- Required input `deliverable_use_case` (`string`): Whether the output is a final hero still, lookdev preview, animation turntable, or baked GLB source
- Required input `optical_feature_requirements` (`array`): Required optical features (refraction, caustics, Volumetrics, SSS, soft area shadows)
- Required input `render_time_and_hardware_budget` (`string`): Per-frame render time ceiling and available GPU/CPU compute posture
- Optional input `blender_version_token` (`string`): Target Blender version governing BLENDER_EEVEE vs BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT naming
- Output contract: `selected_render_engine_record`, `sample_and_denoiser_targets`, `engine_tradeoff_and_fallback_caveats` (Runtime status: `Not Run`, Artifact status: `Not Produced`, `downgrade_only`).

## Quick-start steps
1. Name the use case (hero / preview / animation / lookdev / flat clay).
2. Evaluate required rendering features (caustics / subsurface scattering / volumetrics / global illumination accuracy).
3. Evaluate time budget per frame and available hardware.
4. Pick the engine: `Cycles`, `Eevee`, or `Workbench` (note: Eevee used the name Eevee Next and token `BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT` on Blender 4.2–4.x only; it is `Eevee` with token `BLENDER_EEVEE` on 4.0–4.1 and 5.x).
5. Pin the 4-item engine record: engine + samples + GPU device (if applicable) + caveats.

## Cross-skill handoffs
- [upstream_reference] Lighting and material setup aligned with engine choice → `blender-lighting-material-planner` (`references/skill-blender-lighting-material-planner.md`) — `when.all: [brief.locked equals true; stage.current equals "lookdev_planning"]`
- [upstream_reference] Color configuration decision → `color-management-decision` (`references/skill-color-management-decision.md`) — `when.all: [decision.colorLocked equals false]`

- [upstream_reference] Render resolution and aspect ratio decision → `resolution-aspect-decision` (`references/skill-resolution-aspect-decision.md`) — `when.all: [decision.aspectLocked equals false]`

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- Runtime boundary: Decision skill — does not run Blender. Pins config; operator applies in scene render properties.
- Never run Blender or execute a render or preview render.
- Never configure denoiser specifics, tile sizes, light probe volumes, or render-setting optimizations beyond `engine + samples + GPU device + caveats`.
- Never decide color management (`color-management-decision`), container/codec (`output-format-decision`), or resolution/aspect (`resolution-aspect-decision`).
- Never verify rendered files (`render-export-evidence`).
